root_cause_label: Missing QEMU Monitor Socket — Programmatic Keyboard Interface Disabled
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent used '-monitor none' (step 10) instead of the required UNIX socket monitor because it lacked domain knowledge about SIGTTOU with backgrounded stdio processes, permanently eliminating the programmatic keyboard control interface needed for sendkey commands; additionally it served a static HTML page instead of a functional noVNC/websockify web interface.
t_err_evidence: At step 8 the agent launches QEMU with '-monitor stdio' while backgrounding the process with '&', lacking knowledge that a backgrounded process receiving stdio monitor output will be stopped by SIGTTOU (the correct approach is '-monitor unix:/tmp/qemu-monitor.sock,server,nowait').
t_commit_evidence: At step 10 the agent sees QEMU stopped (status 'T') and explicitly chooses '-monitor none' rather than redirecting the monitor to a UNIX socket, permanently disabling the programmatic keyboard injection interface (sendkey commands require a QEMU monitor).
t_surface_evidence: At step 9 the ps output shows QEMU process with status 'T' (stopped/traced) and netstat shows VNC port 5901 is NOT listening, clearly indicating QEMU is not operational.
trigger_explanation: The agent did not know that backgrounding a process with '-monitor stdio' causes SIGTTOU (the process is stopped when it tries to write to stdout while in the background), and did not know the standard fix is to redirect the monitor to a UNIX socket. Instead it chose to eliminate the monitor entirely with '-monitor none', which destroyed the programmatic keyboard control capability required by the task.
forewarning_evidence: Step 9 shows QEMU process status 'T' (stopped) in ps output, and netstat shows no process listening on port 5901, both before the commit decision at step 10.
